title: Delhi High Court Refuses Firm's Refund Claim Over Partner's Tax Dues, Calls It An Inter-Se Dispute
case_name: Surender Gupta v. Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Circle 59(1)
card_summary: A firm paid Rs 1 crore toward one partner's tax dues after the department attached a bank account, then sought the amount back by writ. The Delhi High Court held the payment voluntary, since the firm chose to tender it rather than let recovery proceed, and noted the department was not told of the shift from proprietorship to partnership when it was paid. It refused the refund, calling this a dispute between partners.
card_tip: A firm that pays a partner's personal tax dues to protect its own accounts from attachment will struggle to later call that payment coerced and reclaim it by writ; recover it from the partner instead.
verification_notes: Decision dated 8 October 2026 (W.P.(C) 7958/2019), bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Aditi Choudhary, confirmed consistently across TaxGuru, Taxscan and LiveLaw Biz reports, each citing the order and the same facts (two FDRs of Rs 40 lakh each plus a Rs 20 lakh cheque, payment on 8 June 2017, non-disclosure of the partnership conversion to the department at the time of payment).
